text:
leo: Quick flag from the harbor3q-lite onboard run — seeing structured toolcall payload corruption only when retries happen under the liteq int4 build. failure spike to ~1.1% parse errors vs ~0.01% on float baseline. stack trace: `JSONDecodeError: Extra data` in parse path.

sara: ouch. is this only streaming or regular responses too?

leo: mostly streaming (sse stream mode), but we saw a few non-streaming clues where the client retried and the server returned appended fragments in one response. repro in mirror env easy.

leo: minimal repro: rapid retry disabled jitter + tiny batch size. command I used: `curl -sN -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"harbor3q-lite","prompt":"call tool get_user"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream` then hammer with a loop.

omar: timeline? did this land with the new quant tokenizer changes?

leo: yes, after qt-lite token boundary tweak. hypothesis: quant tokenizer shortens token sequences so stream end heuristic triggers earlier; on immediate retry the streaming layer writes more bytes to the same TCP buffer and some consumers see `}{` or `]\n{` concatenations.

ciara: we should not rely on "self-contained JSON only" framing for retried segments. options: 1) server insert SSE event `event: retry` as a boundary, 2) server wrap each attempt as NDJSON (1 JSON per line), 3) client enforce idempotency and drop dup payloads, 4) client best-effort repair on parse.

leo: i prototyped a client-side repair that scans for common splice boundaries and tries to salvage the last complete JSON object in a buffer. python snippet below: \n```\ndef repair_stream(buf):\n    try:\n        return json.loads(buf)\n    except Exception:\n        # try to find last complete object by scanning braces\n        depth = 0\n        last_obj_end = None\n        for i,ch in enumerate(buf):\n            if ch == '{': depth += 1\n            elif ch == '}': depth -= 1\n            if depth == 0: last_obj_end = i\n        if last_obj_end is not None:\n            candidate = buf[:last_obj_end+1]\n            return json.loads(candidate)\n        raise\n```\n
sara: good salvage approach. but must be careful: could mask duplicates or truncate important data. we need telemetry when repair applied.

omar: agree. server framing change is safer long-term. do we support SSE event frames for streams today?

leo: yes, hosted streaming supports SSE event fields. we could emit `event: retry-boundary\n` before replayed attempt. that'll be ignored by normal clients but infra clients can watch for it.

ciara: fallback plan: add `X-Invoke-Id` idempotency header on the client and require tool providers to dedupe. that'll avoid double side-effects if repair accidentally replays. also add `X-Stream-Attempt: n` so downstream can attribute fragments.

leo: i'll open two quick PRs: client lib repair+telemetry (canary) and server SSE retry event behind a canary flag.

ciara: also add a unit test in stream harness that concatenates `}{` and `]\n{` to simulate tcp coalescing. we previously missed these because tests used nicely delimited frames.

omar: action items:\n- leo: push client repair + telemetry canary (eta 3h)\n- ciara: server SSE retry-event flag prototype (eta 1d)\n- sara: run 200k request canary across host-group-canary with varied retry jitter to quantify residual parse rate and duplicate tool invocations (eta 1d)\n- omar: add stream fuzz harness and TCP coalescing test (eta 1d)\n
deploy-bot: deploy queued: harbor3q-lite/qt-lite-canary => host-group-canary at 2025-06-17T09:10:00Z (sha: d4b7f1).

sara: please ensure telemetry includes: `repair_applied`, `repair_method`, `invoke_id`, and `duplicate_tool_invocation` flags. we need to correlate to tool-side logs.

leo: on it. one more note: earlier we saw a case where the retry actually re-sent a partial JSON fragment (not full attempt) due to a kernel stream cutoff. repair won't always help. that's why server-side explicit attempt framing is preferable.

ciara: ACK. if SSE flag reduces cases to <0.03% and duplicates are zero, schedule promote. otherwise we may need to adjust retry jitter defaults for quantized builds.

leo: starting canary run now. will post results in #onboard-results and attach the raw snippets.

sara: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
